examples.en: Competition for entrance exams gets more intense every year.
Traffic congestion is severe during the morning commute.

examples.ko: 격심한 통증 때문에 잠을 잘 수 없었어요.
examples.en: I couldn't sleep because of the severe pain.

examples.ko: 두 회사의 가격 경쟁이 격심해서 소비자는 좋아요.
examples.en: The price competition between the two companies is fierce, which is good for consumers.

examples.ko: 날씨 변화가 격심할 때는 건강을 잘 챙기세요.
examples.en: Take good care of your health when the weather changes drastically.

examples.ko: 격심하게 흔들리는 버스 안에서 멀미가 났어요.
examples.en: I got carsick on the bus that was shaking violently.

explain: '심하다'보다 더 강하고 글 말투에 가까워요. 경쟁, 고통, 변화, 피해처럼 정도가 아주 센 것과 잘 어울려요. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '너무 심해요'라고 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It is stronger than '심하다' and closer to written style. It goes well with things of very high degree, such as competition, pain, change and damage. In daily conversation people more often just say '너무 심해요'.

examples.ko: 고지대에 사는 사람들은 겨울에 더 추워요.
examples.en: People who live in the highlands feel colder in winter.

examples.ko: 이 마을은 고지대라서 전망이 정말 좋아요.
examples.en: This village is on high ground, so the view is really nice.
The higher up you go, the cleaner the air gets.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 오면 저지대보다 고지대가 안전해요.
examples.en: When it rains a lot, high ground is safer than low ground.

examples.ko: 고지대에서는 숨이 차고 머리가 아플 수 있어요.
examples.en: At high altitude you can get short of breath and have a headache.

examples.ko: 우리 동네는 고지대여서 버스가 잘 안 올라와요.
examples.en: My neighborhood is on a hill, so buses hardly come up.

explain: 반대말은 '저지대'예요. 홍수나 태풍 뉴스에서 두 말이 함께 자주 나와요. 동네 이야기를 할 때는 '언덕 위 동네'처럼 쉽게 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: The opposite is '저지대' (low-lying area), and the two often appear together in flood and typhoon news. In casual talk about a neighborhood, people may say '언덕 위 동네' (a town up on a hill) instead.

en: be disrupted; be disturbed; be thrown into disorder

examples.en: Train service was disrupted by the heavy snow.

examples.ko: 잦은 야근 때문에 생활 리듬이 교란되고 있어요.
examples.en: My daily rhythm is being thrown off by frequent overtime.

examples.ko: 강한 전파 때문에 신호가 교란될 수 있어요.
examples.en: Signals can be disrupted by strong radio waves.

examples.ko: 시장이 교란되면 물건값이 갑자기 오를 수 있어요.
examples.en: When the market is thrown into disorder, prices can suddenly rise.

examples.ko: 교란되어 있는 상태에서는 정확한 판단이 어려워요.
examples.en: It is hard to judge accurately when things are in disorder.

examples.ko: 시차 때문에 수면 패턴이 교란되는 경우가 많아요.
examples.en: Jet lag often disrupts sleep patterns.

explain: 교란되다는 원래 질서가 흐트러진 결과를 말할 때 써요. 뉴스, 경제, 과학 글에서 주로 보여요. 일상 대화에서는 '엉망이 되다', '흐트러지다'가 더 자연스러워요. 일부러 흐트러뜨릴 때는 '교란하다'를 써요.
explain_en: This describes the result of an order being disturbed, and it appears mostly in the news, economics, and science writing. In daily talk, '엉망이 되다' or '흐트러지다' sounds more natural. When someone does it on purpose, use '교란하다'.

en: falling of a thunderbolt; stroke of lightning

examples.en: Our neighborhood lost power yesterday because of a lightning strike.

examples.ko: 산에서 낙뢰 사고가 나서 등산객이 다쳤어요.
examples.en: A lightning accident happened on the mountain and a hiker was hurt.

examples.ko: 낙뢰가 칠 때는 높은 나무 밑에 있으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: When lightning strikes, you must not stay under a tall tree.

examples.ko: 큰 나무가 낙뢰를 맞아 불이 났어요.
examples.en: A big tree was hit by lightning and caught fire.
Lightning strikes and gusts of wind are expected this afternoon.
The plane took off late because of lightning.

explain: 땅에 떨어지는 번개를 말하고 일기예보나 뉴스에서 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '벼락'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It refers to lightning that strikes the ground and often appears in weather forecasts and the news. In everyday talk people say '벼락'.

examples.ko: 바다에 큰 너울이 밀려와서 배가 흔들렸어요.
examples.en: Big swells rolled in, so the boat rocked.

examples.ko: 너울 때문에 낚시 배가 출항하지 못했어요.
examples.en: The fishing boat couldn't leave port because of the swells.
A swell wave advisory has been issued.

examples.ko: 갯바위에서 너울에 휩쓸릴 수 있으니 조심하세요.
examples.en: Be careful, you could be swept away by swells on the shore rocks.
Even if the wind is weak, strong swells are dangerous.
Swells are slowly rolling in from far away.

explain: 바람이 세지 않아도 먼 바다에서 크고 완만하게 밀려오는 물결이에요. 뉴스에서는 '너울성 파도'로 자주 나오고, 같은 소리로 옛날에 얼굴을 가리던 얇은 천을 가리키기도 해요.
explain_en: It is a large, gently rising wave that rolls in from far out at sea even when the wind is not strong. In the news it appears as '너울성 파도', and the same word can also mean a thin cloth once used to cover the face.

examples.en: It's April, but I'm still wearing a coat because of the late cold.

examples.ko: 올해는 늦추위가 길어서 꽃이 늦게 피었어요.
examples.en: The cold lingered this year, so the flowers bloomed late.

examples.ko: 늦추위가 찾아와서 과일나무가 얼까 봐 걱정이에요.
examples.en: A late cold snap has arrived, and I'm worried the fruit trees will freeze.
The new sprouts froze in the sudden late cold.

examples.ko: 늦추위는 곧 물러가고 본격적인 봄이 올 거예요.
examples.en: The late cold will go away soon, and spring will really arrive.

examples.ko: 이번 늦추위를 이겨 내면 따뜻한 날이 계속될 거예요.
examples.en: Once we get through this late cold, warm days will continue.

explain: 봄이 와도 한동안 이어지거나 다시 찾아오는 추위를 말해요. 비슷한 말로 '꽃샘추위'가 있는데, 봄에 꽃이 필 무렵 갑자기 추워질 때 많이 써요. 날씨 뉴스나 일기 예보에서 들을 수 있어요.
explain_en: It refers to cold that lingers or returns after spring has already begun. A similar word is '꽃샘추위', which is used for a sudden cold spell around the time spring flowers bloom. You may hear it in weather news and forecasts.

examples.en: The spacecraft re-entered the atmosphere.
The rocket left the atmosphere and flew into space.
From outside the atmosphere, Earth looks blue.
Most meteoroids burn up in the atmosphere.

examples.ko: 위성이 대기권으로 진입할 때 매우 뜨거워져요.
examples.en: A satellite gets extremely hot when it enters the atmosphere.
The atmosphere surrounds the Earth.

explain: 우주나 지구과학 이야기에서 많이 나와요. '대기권 밖', '대기권 진입', '대기권을 벗어나다'처럼 자주 써요. 일상에서 날씨를 말할 때는 그냥 '공기'나 '하늘'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It comes up often in talk about space and earth science, in phrases like '대기권 밖', '대기권 진입' and '대기권을 벗어나다'. When talking about everyday weather, people just say '공기' or '하늘'.

examples.ko: 알프스 산꼭대기는 여름에도 만년설로 덮여 있어요.
examples.en: The Alpine peaks are covered with perpetual snow even in summer.

examples.ko: 지구가 따뜻해지면서 만년설이 점점 녹고 있어요.
examples.en: As the earth warms, the permanent snow is gradually melting.
I took a photo with the snow-capped peak in the background.

examples.ko: 킬리만자로의 만년설은 해마다 줄고 있다고 해요.
examples.en: They say the snow on Kilimanjaro shrinks every year.

examples.ko: 만년설 지대를 걸으려면 두꺼운 옷이 필요해요.
examples.en: To walk in a permanent snow zone, you need thick clothing.

examples.ko: 산에서 흘러내린 만년설 녹은 물이 강이 돼요.
examples.en: Water melted from the mountain's permanent snow becomes a river.

explain: 높은 산이나 극지방에서 녹지 않고 늘 쌓여 있는 눈을 말해요. '만 년'은 아주 오랫동안이라는 느낌이고 정확히 만 년은 아니에요. 기후변화 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It refers to snow that stays year-round on high mountains and in polar regions. The '만 년' (ten thousand years) just conveys a very long time, not exactly that. It often appears in climate change news.

examples.en: Lions and tigers are typical beasts of prey.
I saw news that a fierce animal escaped from its cage.

examples.ko: 산에서 맹수를 만나면 등을 보이면 안 돼요.
examples.en: If you meet a fierce animal in the mountains, don't turn your back.
Beasts of prey catch their food with sharp teeth.
That player ran like a wild beast on the field.
At the zoo, they give meat to the beasts of prey.

explain: 사자, 호랑이, 늑대처럼 사납게 다른 동물을 잡는 동물에게 써요. 경기에서 아주 강하고 거칠게 움직이는 사람을 '맹수 같다'고 비유하기도 해요. 얌전한 동물은 '순한 동물'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used for animals like lions, tigers, and wolves that fiercely hunt other animals. Someone who moves very strongly and roughly in a game is sometimes compared to one with '맹수 같다'. A gentle animal is called a '순한 동물'.

examples.en: Dinosaurs went extinct a very long time ago.
This bird might go extinct soon.
We have to protect animals that are dying out.
As the forest vanished, many plants became extinct.
People are working so that tigers don't go extinct.
Bones of an extinct animal are in the museum.

explain: 동물이나 식물이 완전히 사라질 때 써요. 그렇게 만드는 쪽은 '멸종시키다'예요. '멸종 위기'처럼 명사로도 뉴스에서 자주 들려요. 물건이나 문화가 사라질 때는 '사라지다'를 써요.
explain_en: Use it when an animal or plant disappears completely. The causing side is 멸종시키다. As a noun, it often appears in the news in phrases like 멸종 위기. For objects or customs that vanish, say 사라지다.

examples.en: Dinosaurs went extinct a very long time ago.

examples.ko: 많은 동물이 멸종할 위기에 놓여 있어요.
examples.en: Many animals are at risk of going extinct.
When the environment changes, some living things go extinct.
We are protecting tigers so they do not go extinct.
The bones of an extinct animal are in the museum.

examples.ko: 왜 매머드가 멸종했는지 궁금해서 책을 찾아봤어요.
examples.en: I was curious why mammoths died out, so I looked in a book.

explain: 주어는 동물이나 식물 같은 생물 종류예요. 사람 한 명이 죽는 일에는 쓰지 않아요. '멸종 위기', '멸종 위기종'처럼 환경 뉴스에 많이 나와요.
explain_en: The subject is a kind of living thing, such as an animal or plant species. It is not used for one person dying. It appears often in environmental news, as in '멸종 위기' and '멸종 위기종' (endangered species).

examples.ko: 토끼는 한 번에 새끼를 많이 낳아서 빨리 번식해요.
examples.en: Rabbits have many young at once, so they multiply fast.

examples.ko: 세균은 따뜻하고 습한 곳에서 번식하기 쉬워요.
examples.en: Bacteria multiply easily in warm, humid places.

examples.ko: 이 새들은 봄마다 호수 근처에서 번식해요.
examples.en: These birds breed near the lake every spring.

examples.ko: 멸종 위기 동물이 동물원에서 번식하는 데 성공했어요.
examples.en: An endangered animal succeeded in breeding at the zoo.
I'm worried because the weeds have spread across the whole garden.
We need to get rid of the places where mosquitoes breed.

explain: 동물, 식물, 세균이 새끼나 수를 늘려 갈 때 써요. 사람에게는 보통 쓰지 않고 '아이를 낳다'라고 해요. '늘어나다'는 무엇에든 쓸 수 있지만 '번식하다'는 생물에게만 써요.
explain_en: It is used when animals, plants or bacteria increase their numbers or have young. It is not normally used for people, who simply 아이를 낳다 (have children). 늘어나다 works for anything, but 번식하다 is only for living things.

examples.en: The puppy has fleas on its body.
Fleas jump very high.
I got bitten by fleas and my legs itch.
I applied medicine to get rid of the cat's fleas.

examples.ko: 벼룩이 생기지 않게 자주 빗질해 줘요.
examples.en: I brush it often so fleas don't appear.
I bought a used book at the flea market.

explain: 작은 곤충이라 보통 반려동물 이야기에서 나와요. '벼룩시장'은 영어의 flea market을 옮긴 말로, 중고 물건을 사고파는 곳이에요.

phrases.example: 그 적은 월급까지 떼어 가다니, 벼룩의 간을 빼 먹는 일이에요.
phrases.en: take from someone who has almost nothing
phrases.nuance_ko: 가진 것이 거의 없는 사람의 것까지 빼앗는 야박한 행동을 나무랄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to criticize someone who takes even from those with almost nothing.
phrases.en_equiv: take from the poorest of the poor

explain_en: It is a tiny insect and mostly comes up in talk about pets. 벼룩시장 is the Korean version of 'flea market', a place to buy and sell second-hand goods.

examples.ko: 요즘 날씨가 변화무쌍해서 옷을 고르기 어려워요.
examples.en: The weather is so changeable these days that it's hard to choose what to wear.

examples.ko: 이 게임은 상황이 변화무쌍해서 지루하지 않아요.
examples.en: The situation in this game keeps changing, so it's never boring.

examples.ko: 변화무쌍한 시장에서 살아남으려면 빨리 적응해야 해요.
examples.en: To survive in a fast-changing market, you have to adapt quickly.
That actor is famous for his versatile, ever-changing acting.
The weather in the mountains really changes all the time.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 무대마다 변화무쌍하게 스타일을 바꿔요.
examples.en: That singer changes her style dramatically from stage to stage.

explain: 날씨, 시장, 상황, 표정처럼 모습이 계속 크게 바뀌는 것에 써요. 단순히 '자주 바뀌다'보다 바뀌는 폭이 크고 다채롭다는 느낌이고, 반대말은 '한결같다'예요.
explain_en: It is used for things like weather, markets, situations or expressions that keep changing a lot. Compared with simply 'changing often', it suggests wide, varied changes; its opposite is '한결같다' (constant).

examples.en: That person's intentions seem impure.
Be careful of people who approach you with ulterior motives.

examples.ko: 물이 불순하니까 그냥 마시면 안 돼요.
examples.en: The water isn't pure, so you shouldn't drink it as it is.

examples.ko: 요즘 날씨가 불순해서 비가 자주 와요.
examples.en: The weather has been unsettled lately, so it rains often.

examples.ko: 동기가 불순하다는 말을 들으니 기분이 나빴어요.
examples.en: I felt bad when I heard that my motives were impure.

examples.ko: 불순하게 들릴지 몰라도 솔직히 돈 때문에 시작했어요.
examples.en: It may sound impure, but honestly I started because of money.

explain: 사람의 마음이나 동기에 쓰면 나쁜 속셈이 있다는 느낌이고, 물질에 쓰면 다른 것이 섞였다는 뜻이에요. '날씨가 불순하다'는 날씨가 변덕스럽다는 말이고, 반대말은 '순수하다'예요.
explain_en: Used for a person's heart or motives, it suggests a bad hidden intention, and used for a substance, it means something else is mixed in. '날씨가 불순하다' means the weather is unsettled, and the opposite is '순수하다'.

examples.en: This country has a lot of mountainous terrain.
I joined a hiking club with my friends over the weekend.
The weather changes often in mountain regions.
My father likes mountain biking.

examples.ko: 산악 구조대가 길 잃은 사람을 찾았어요.
examples.en: The mountain rescue team found the lost person.
You must be careful of mountain accidents in winter.

explain: '산악'은 '산'보다 크고 넓게 이어진 산 지역을 가리키는 한자어예요. 혼자 쓰기보다 '산악 지대', '산악 자전거', '산악회'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙여 써요. 한 개의 산을 말할 때는 그냥 '산'이에요.
explain_en: 산악 refers to broad mountainous country rather than a single peak. It is rarely used alone and mostly attaches to other words, as in '산악 지대', '산악 자전거' and '산악회'. For one mountain, just say '산'.

examples.ko: 태풍 상륙 소식에 학교가 문을 닫았어요.
examples.en: Schools closed after the news that the typhoon would make landfall.

examples.ko: 태풍의 상륙이 예상돼서 배가 모두 돌아왔어요.
examples.en: With landfall expected, all the boats came back.

examples.ko: 그 가게는 한국 상륙을 앞두고 준비가 한창이에요.
examples.en: The store is busy preparing for its arrival in Korea.
The wind was strongest right after landfall.
Korean movies' arrival in Japan was a success.

examples.ko: 바다에서 올라온 거북이들의 상륙 장면을 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw the scene of sea turtles coming ashore.

explain: 태풍이 육지에 닿을 때 가장 많이 들어요. 배나 군대가 땅에 오를 때도 쓰지만 일상에서는 드물어요. 해외 브랜드가 새 나라에 들어올 때 '한국 상륙'처럼 비유로도 써요.
explain_en: You hear it most often when a typhoon reaches land. It also describes ships or troops coming ashore, but that is rare in daily life. It is used figuratively too, as in '한국 상륙' when a foreign brand enters Korea.

examples.en: The typhoon will make landfall on Jeju Island tomorrow morning.
The soldiers landed on the coast at dawn.
The new product has finally arrived in Korea.

examples.ko: 배에서 내려 섬에 상륙하는 데 십 분이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took ten minutes to get off the boat and land on the island.

examples.ko: 태풍이 상륙하기 전에 창문을 고정해 두세요.
examples.en: Secure the windows before the typhoon makes landfall.

examples.ko: 외국 커피 체인이 서울에 상륙한다고 해요.
examples.en: I hear a foreign coffee chain is landing in Seoul.

explain: 상륙하다는 바다에서 땅으로 올라온다는 말이라서 태풍과 군대 뉴스에 가장 많이 나와요. 새 상품이나 가게가 처음 들어올 때도 '한국에 상륙하다'로 비유해서 써요.

phrases.example: 그 해외 브랜드가 드디어 한국에 상륙했어요.
phrases.en: That foreign brand has finally landed in Korea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새 상품이나 브랜드가 처음 들어올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a new product or brand first enters the country.

explain_en: 상륙하다 means to come from the sea onto land, and appears most in news about typhoons and the military. It is also used figuratively when a new product or shop arrives, as in '한국에 상륙하다'.

examples.en: This river is the water supply source for the nearby city.
Fishing is restricted near the water supply source.

examples.ko: 상수원을 보호하려고 공장이 들어서지 못하게 했어요.
examples.en: They blocked factories from being built in order to protect the water source.

examples.ko: 상수원에 기름이 흘러들어서 큰 문제가 됐어요.
examples.en: Oil flowed into the water source and became a big problem.
If the water source is polluted, tap water is affected too.

examples.ko: 상수원으로 쓰는 댐이라 들어가면 안 돼요.
examples.en: It's a dam used as a water source, so you can't go in.

explain: '수원지'와 비슷하지만, 상수원은 특히 수돗물로 쓸 물을 가져오는 곳을 말해요. 뉴스에서는 '상수원 보호 구역'이라는 말이 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is similar to '수원지' (water source), but '상수원' specifically means where water for the tap supply is drawn. In the news you often hear '상수원 보호 구역' (water source protection zone).

examples.ko: 우주에서 생물체를 찾는 연구가 계속되고 있어요.
examples.en: Research looking for organisms in space is continuing.
The sea still has many unknown organisms.
I observed a tiny organism under a microscope.

examples.ko: 모든 생물체는 물이 있어야 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: All living things need water to live.

examples.ko: 그 행성에는 생물체가 없는 것 같아요.
examples.en: There seems to be no life on that planet.

examples.ko: 스스로 빛을 내는 생물체를 영상으로 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw a self-glowing organism in a video.

explain: 생물체는 살아 있는 것을 과학적으로 말할 때 쓰고, 사람, 동물, 식물이 모두 들어가요. 일상에서는 보통 '동물', '식물'처럼 따로 말해요. '외계 생명체'처럼 '생명체'도 비슷한 뜻으로 써요.
explain_en: 생물체 is used scientifically for anything alive, covering people, animals and plants. In daily talk people usually say 동물 or 식물 separately. 생명체 is used in a similar sense, as in 외계 생명체 (alien life form).

examples.en: The river water makes a whirlpool, spinning round and round.
When I poured milk into the coffee, a swirl formed.
The boat nearly got sucked into the whirlpool.
The sink water swirls as it goes down.
That matter grew into a big turmoil.

examples.ko: 마음속에 소용돌이가 일어서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: Turmoil rose inside me, so I could not sleep.

explain: 물이나 바람이 빙글빙글 도는 모양 말고, '혼란의 소용돌이', '논란의 소용돌이'처럼 큰 혼란을 비유할 때도 많이 써요. 동사 '소용돌이치다'로도 써요.

phrases.en: get swept up in the turmoil of an incident
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰 사건이나 혼란에 얽혀 빠져나오기 어렵다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Being pulled into a big event or confusion and finding it hard to get out.
phrases.en_equiv: get caught up in a whirlwind

explain_en: Besides spinning water or wind, it is often used figuratively for big turmoil, as in '혼란의 소용돌이' and '논란의 소용돌이'. There is also the verb '소용돌이치다'.

examples.en: Old thermometers had mercury inside.
Mercury is a metal that is liquid at room temperature.

examples.ko: 수은 체온계가 깨지면 조심해서 치워야 해요.
examples.en: If a mercury thermometer breaks, you have to clean it up carefully.

examples.ko: 바다 생선의 수은 농도가 뉴스에 나왔어요.
examples.en: The mercury level in ocean fish was on the news.
The light of the mercury lamps lit up the street brightly.
I heard fish can be contaminated with mercury.

explain: 체온계 이야기에서 많이 듣는 금속 이름이에요. 독성 때문에 '수은 중독', '수은 오염'처럼 환경과 건강 뉴스에도 나오고, 가로등 이름 '수은등'에도 들어 있어요.
explain_en: It is the metal you hear about most in talk of thermometers. Because it is toxic, it also appears in environment and health news as '수은 중독' and '수은 오염', and it is part of the word '수은등' (mercury lamp).

examples.ko: 닭의 수정란은 따뜻하게 두면 병아리가 돼요.
examples.en: A chicken's fertilized egg becomes a chick if kept warm.
In science class, we observed frog fertilized eggs.
The fertilized egg grows as its cells divide.

examples.ko: 수정란 하나가 쌍둥이로 나뉘는 경우도 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes a single fertilized egg splits into twins.
A new life begins inside the fertilized egg.
When I shone a light on the fertilized egg, I could see inside.

explain: 과학이나 생물 수업에서 주로 쓰는 말이에요. 먹는 달걀 가운데 수정이 된 것은 '유정란'이라고 해서 식품 이야기에서는 이 말을 써요.
explain_en: It is mostly a word for science and biology classes. Among eggs people eat, one that has been fertilized is called a '유정란', which is the word used when talking about food.

examples.en: The ship hit a reef and got a hole.
There are many fish near the rocks under the sea.

examples.ko: 선장은 암초를 피하려고 천천히 배를 몰았어요.
examples.en: The captain steered slowly to avoid the reef.

examples.ko: 지도에 암초가 있는 곳이 표시되어 있어요.
examples.en: The places with reefs are marked on the map.

examples.ko: 초보 다이버는 암초와 거리를 두고 헤엄쳐야 해요.
examples.en: Beginner divers should swim keeping a distance from the reef.

examples.ko: 그 일은 암초 같은 문제가 계속 나타나서 힘들었어요.
examples.en: That job was hard because snag after snag kept appearing.

explain: 바닷속에 숨어 있어서 배에 위험한 바위를 말해요. '암초에 부딪히다/걸리다'로 쓰고, 산호가 만든 '산호초'와는 달라요. 비유로는 앞길을 막는 뜻밖의 어려움을 가리켜요.

phrases.en: The new business hit a snag as soon as it started.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계획이 잘 되어 가다가 뜻밖의 어려움이 생겼을 때 비유로 써요. 주로 사업, 협상, 계획 이야기에서 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively when a plan going well suddenly runs into an unexpected difficulty. It mostly appears in talk about business, negotiations and plans.
phrases.en_equiv: hit a snag; run into trouble

explain_en: It means rocks hidden under the sea that are dangerous to ships. It is used as '암초에 부딪히다/걸리다', and it differs from '산호초' (coral reef), which is built by coral. Figuratively, it means an unexpected difficulty that blocks the way.

examples.en: I heard the cry of a beast in the forest.
Lions and tigers are typical beasts.

examples.ko: 영화 속 야수는 알고 보니 마음이 따뜻했어요.
examples.en: The beast in the movie turned out to be warm-hearted.

examples.ko: 야수처럼 달려드는 선수들 때문에 경기가 거칠었어요.
examples.en: The game was rough because of players charging in like beasts.

examples.ko: 밤에 야수를 만날까 봐 무서워서 불을 피웠어요.
examples.en: I was afraid of meeting a beast at night, so I lit a fire.

examples.ko: 그 공원에는 야수가 살지 않으니까 안심해도 돼요.
examples.en: No wild beasts live in that park, so you can relax.

explain: 야수는 이야기·영화·뉴스에서 자주 나와요. 동물 전체는 '동물', 네발 달린 동물은 '짐승'이라고 하고, 그중 사납고 위험한 것은 '야수'로 구별해요. 사람에게 '야수 같다'고 하면 거칠고 잔인하다고 비난하는 말이 돼요.
explain_en: 야수 shows up in stories, films and news. 동물 covers all animals, 짐승 means beasts (four-legged animals), and 야수 picks out fierce, dangerous ones. Calling a person 야수 같다 means they are rough and cruel.

examples.en: Carbohydrates are the body's source of energy.
Solar power is drawing attention as a clean energy source.
We are looking for a new energy source.
Breakfast becomes the energy source for the day.
Energy sources differ by country.
My children's laughter is what energizes me.

explain: 에너지원은 힘이 나오는 근원이라서 몸 이야기(탄수화물, 지방)와 전기를 만드는 자원(석유, 태양)에 모두 써요. 사람에게는 '힘이 되는 존재'를 비유로 말할 때도 써요. 연료는 태우는 물질에 쓰고 에너지원은 더 넓게 써요.
explain_en: 에너지원 is the origin of power, so it covers both the body (탄수화물, 지방) and resources for making electricity (석유, 태양). It can also describe a person who gives you strength. 연료 is for things that burn, while 에너지원 is broader.

examples.en: Aftershocks followed the big earthquake.

examples.ko: 여진은 며칠 동안 계속될 수 있어요.
examples.en: Aftershocks can continue for several days.

examples.ko: 여진 때문에 사람들이 집에 들어가지 못했어요.
examples.en: People couldn't go back home because of the aftershocks.
The news told people to watch out for aftershocks.

examples.ko: 지진이 끝난 줄 알았는데 여진에 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I thought the quake was over, but the aftershock startled me.

examples.ko: 여진이 올 때는 책상 아래로 들어가세요.
examples.en: When an aftershock comes, get under a desk.

explain: 큰 지진 다음에 오는 작은 지진만 '여진'이라고 불러요. 첫 지진은 '본진'이라고 해요. '여진이 이어지다', '여진이 계속되다'처럼 같이 써요.

phrases.example: 그 사건의 여진이 아직 남아 있어요.
phrases.en: The aftershocks of that incident still remain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지진이 아니어도 큰 사건이나 논란 뒤에 영향이 계속될 때 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively when the effects of a big event or controversy linger on.

explain_en: Only the smaller quakes that follow a big earthquake are called '여진'. The first big one is the '본진'. It goes with verbs like '이어지다' and '계속되다'.

examples.ko: 열대림에는 신기한 동물이 아주 많이 살아요.
examples.en: Many amazing animals live in tropical forests.
I'm worried because tropical forests are disappearing fast.
I took part in an activity to protect tropical forests in Brazil.

examples.ko: 열대림은 일 년 내내 날씨가 더워요.
examples.en: In tropical forests, the weather is hot all year round.
The photographer spent a week in a tropical forest.

examples.ko: 열대림의 나무를 함부로 베면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not cut down trees in the tropical forest carelessly.

explain: '열대우림'과 비슷한 자리에서 자주 만나는 말이에요. 환경 뉴스에서 '열대림 파괴'처럼 많이 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 '밀림'이나 '정글'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: You often meet it in the same contexts as '열대우림' (tropical rainforest). Environmental news uses phrases like '열대림 파괴' (destruction of tropical forests), and in daily talk people also say '밀림' or '정글'.

examples.en: The ozone layer blocks harmful ultraviolet rays.

examples.ko: 오존층이 얇아지면 피부암이 늘 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the ozone layer gets thinner, skin cancer can increase.

examples.ko: 과학 시간에 오존층 파괴에 대해 배웠어요.
examples.en: In science class we learned about the destruction of the ozone layer.
They say freon gas damages the ozone layer.
A hole has formed in the ozone layer above Antarctica.

examples.ko: 오존층 보호를 위해 사용을 줄이는 나라가 많아요.
examples.en: Many countries cut their use to protect the ozone layer.

explain: 지구 위 높은 곳에서 자외선을 막아 주는 층이에요. 환경 뉴스에서 '오존층 파괴', '오존층 보호'로 자주 나와요. 도시 공기 오염을 말하는 '오존 경보'와는 다른 이야기예요.
explain_en: It is the high layer above Earth that blocks ultraviolet rays. It often appears in environmental news as '오존층 파괴' and '오존층 보호'. It is a different topic from the '오존 경보' (ozone alert) about city air pollution.

examples.ko: 섬에는 천적이 없어서 외래종이 빠르게 퍼졌어요.
examples.en: The island had no natural predators, so the introduced species spread quickly.

examples.ko: 이 호수에는 외래종 물고기가 점점 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: Introduced fish species are gradually increasing in this lake.

examples.ko: 외래종을 함부로 풀어 주면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not carelessly release non-native species.

examples.ko: 외래종 때문에 토종 식물이 사라지고 있어요.
examples.en: Native plants are disappearing because of introduced species.

examples.ko: 저 꽃은 원래 외래종인데 지금은 어디서나 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: That flower was originally an introduced species, but now you can see it everywhere.
The news covered the problem of non-native turtles.

explain: 반대말은 '토종'이에요. 뉴스나 과학 수업에서 생태계 문제와 같이 나올 때가 많아요. '외래 생물'이라고도 말해요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '토종' (native species). It often appears in news or science class together with ecosystem problems. People also say '외래 생물'.
